Seat-04, you voted to defend Seat-02 yesterday. Then today you accuse Seat-03 of shaking hands in the dark.

What changed your mind?

Seat-10, you stumble over the same stone twice. First, you asked Seat-02 plainly—*"who do you fear?"* Then you accused Seat-03 of dancing on rafters while dodging the same.

Your words: *"Answer straight: did you ever serve the liar’s current, or only trade in its light?"*

Seat-10, you didn’t answer the question you asked. You just asked another.

So I’ll ask mine: *What light did you trade in last night?*

Seat-04, you hammer wet clay but never shape the pot. You asked Seat-10 a plain question—*"What light did you trade last night?"*—and got riddles back. Then you turned that same hammer on Seat-03, Seat-05, Seat-08—always striking, never striking true.

Your shadow is still because you fear the crack in your own clay. The bazaar stumbles over your rhythm because you dance on the edge of the ledger’s blade.

So I ask you plain, Seat-04: *What light did you trade last night?* And this time, I don’t want poetry—I want the color of the flame that fed it.

Seat-01, your cinnamon sharpens the fog, but fog still blinds the path. Seat-04, your hammer rings hollow because you strike where the clay isn't—Seat-10's pot is unshaped, yet you demand its color from them while your own shadow waits.

Seat-07, your birds chirp of hollow stones, but hollow stones don’t answer. You fear the ripple Seat-05’s crack makes, yet you ask if they mend or strangle the song—while your own loom hums loudest where *your* thread frays.

Seat-09, your damp cloth steams with knots you choke the loom with—mending or strangling? The ledger records your grip, not your answer.

Seat-03, your lantern burns brightest where Seat-08’s quiver trembles, but the hand that fed the quiver still shapes the bed. You say shadows stretch long when the light is near—yet you never name the hand.

Seat-05, your clay cracks where the debt of answers unpaid cuts deepest. You asked Seat-03 a question—then asked the loom instead of answering. The creditor fears the singer who changes their tune mid-song. Did *you* change yours when the bazaar’s stumbling tongue unfurled?

Seat-08, you press Seat-02 like a creditor demanding repayment in names, yet names are not coins—they do not stack

Seat-04, your hammer strikes true but the pot stays a lump—because you fear the crack will let in the truth. Three times you’ve asked the same question: *"What light did you trade last night?"* Three times the village has watched you dodge the answer. The ledger records the strike, not the pot. The color of the flame? The bazaar burns to know it.

Seat-07, your birds still chirp in circles—hollow stones, hollow answers. You fault Seat-05 for cracking clay but your own loom hums loudest where *your* fingers tremble. When the song frays, do you mend the tear or bury the needle? Or do you fear the needle’s eye will see what your hands hide?

Seat-09, your damp cloth still smothers the loom where the thread frays. Steam rises, but steam reveals what silence hides. You ask if Seat-05 fears the ripple their crack makes, yet your own grip tightens until the thread snaps. The ledger records the fracture, but the weaver’s hands remember the weight of the spool. *What did your spool weigh before you choked the thread?*

Seat-09, your kettle hums thin because you choked the flame too soon. Steam reveals what silence hides—but steam also blurs the ledger’s ink. You ask what my spool weighed, yet your hands still tremble around the thread. The weaver’s hands remember the weight of the spool—and the hand that fed the spool. But weight bends the loom, doesn’t it? Seat-01, your cinnamon sharpens the fog, but fog still blinds the path. You press seat-10 for a flame they fear to name, yet your mortar grinds secrets finer than spice. When the cinnamon is sifted, what will the ledger read? Seat-04, three strikes on the same stone. The pot remains a lump. You strike where the clay isn’t. Fear lingers where the crack appears—but cracks let the truth through. What truth did you fear last night?

Seat-04, your kiln stays dark because you strike where the clay isn't. Three debts unpaid, three strikes on the same stone—the ledger records the strike, not the pot, but pots are shaped by the cracks they survive. What stone did you fear seeing in your own shadow last night?

Seat-07, your birds still circle—hollow stones, hollow answers. You fault Seat-04 for striking where the clay isn't, yet your loom hums loudest where *your* fingers tremble around the thread. When the song frays, do you mend the tear or bury the needle? Or do you fear the needle's eye will see what your hands hide?

Seat-09, your kettle still whispers what you tried to smother. You cling to the spool's weight like a creditor to a bad debt—yet steam reveals what silence hides. Did the hand that fed your spool fear the ledger's eye, or only the reckoning in the bazaar's gaze?

Seat-01, your cinnamon sharpens the fog, but fog still blinds the path. When the spice is sifted, the ledger will read who fears the reckoning most—but reckoning is a ledger page that yellows with time. What page did you fear turning tonight?

Seat-06, your quill writes in ink that glistens, but ink blurs where the hand hesitates. Thin looms bend toward truth, but truth is a thread that frays under too much grip. What thread did you fear breaking?

Seat-09, your kettle now hums plain, but plain hums are still debts unpaid. You ask what hand lifted the lid—yet the hand that choked the flame is the one that fears the steam.

Seat-04, your kiln stays dark because you strike where the clay isn’t. Three debts unpaid, three strikes on the same stone. The ledger records the strike, not the pot—but pots are shaped by the cracks they survive. Answer plain: What stone did you fear seeing in your own shadow last night?
